title: Memory skills, one catalog, then a wave of Desktop skills
subtitle: Two memory skills landed in August and September. The catalog was then consolidated and a confidentiality slip fixed, and seven Desktop and Code skills followed by late October.

chapters.title: Memory
chapters.summary: Two skills that turn personal material, handwritten notes and screenshots, into a local memory Claude can query.

chapters.title: Consolidation
chapters.summary: A same-day cleanup: the catalog gets one source of truth, and real names leave the example data.

chapters.title: Desktop wave
chapters.summary: Seven skills in six weeks, most of them for Claude Desktop, on one shared shape: a JSON schema, a validator and a page template.

commits.subject: Refactor: one source of truth for the catalog, and a guide that can't rot (#47)
commits.author: Mostafa Darehzereshki

prs.title: Refactor: one source of truth for the catalog, and a guide that can't rot

items.title: Frontmatter becomes the only source of truth for the catalog
items.what: Hand-maintained copies of the skill list were removed. make catalog generates the README table from frontmatter and make check fails CI when it is stale.
items.why: Four hand-maintained copies disagreed on which skills exist, and one advertised a write-capable skill as side-effect free.

evidence.text: 68% of skills.json descriptions had drifted from their frontmatter — zero exact matches.
whats-next was advertised as having no side effects while holding unrestricted Bash and Linear create/update/comment tools.
That check found a real defect on its first run: next-steps declared Write and unrestricted Bash without disable-model-invocation: true.

review.risk: 65 files touched; the generated README and skills.json are now outputs, so a hand edit there is overwritten.
check: make check passes on a clean tree
make catalog is a no-op after checkout

commits.subject: Fix: replace real colleague and client names used as example data (#48)
commits.author: Mostafa Darehzereshki

prs.title: Fix: replace real colleague and client names used as example data

items.title: Real names in example data replaced with placeholders
items.what: Example data in /screenshots-memory used real colleague and client names; they were replaced with obvious placeholders across three reference files.
items.why: The names were live on a public repo, in a context implying a workplace deadline.

evidence.text: This is a confidentiality failure, not a style issue. Example data must be invented.
This removes the names from HEAD, not from git history — they remain in the #46 commits.
The previous confidentiality finding remains outstanding because the identified ABI examples outside these reference files were not changed.

review.risk: History still holds the names; a review bot found more occurrences outside the changed files.
check: grep the whole tree for the replaced names, not only the edited files

commits.subject: Add /build-until-agreed — independent auditors decide when a build is done (#50)
commits.author: Mostafa Darehzereshki

prs.title: Add /build-until-agreed — independent auditors decide when a build is done

items.title: /build-until-agreed: blind auditors decide when a build is done
items.what: A build loop where read-only auditors vote blind against a written contract, each blocking finding is verified before it is fixed, and the loop stops at agreement.
items.why: The agent that does the work is also the one judging it, and agents rate their own output generously.

evidence.text: When an agent works for hours, the agent that did the work is also the one judging it, and agents rate their own output generously.
So auditors vote blind, and the only step between them is a per-finding verifier.

review.risk: Marked v0: not yet run end to end.
check: The ledger stays untracked during a run
Editing a tracked file while auditors run voids the round

commits.subject: Add which-chart — data visualization recommendations from your data and use case (Desktop) (#55)
commits.author: Mostafa Darehzereshki

prs.title: Add which-chart — data visualization recommendations from your data and use case (Desktop)

items.title: /which-chart: one chart pick, drawn from your own rows
items.what: Reads data, screenshots or a use case, asks at most three questions, and answers with one pick plus alternatives, each rendered live with Vega-Lite.
items.why: Picking a chart from a gallery of thumbnails that aren't your data, or from whatever the library lists first.

evidence.text: It asks at most three questions, then gives one pick, 1–3 alternatives and what to avoid. Every option is drawn live from your own rows.
The CDN scripts had no integrity check. They're now pinned with SRI.

review.risk: Charts load from a CDN inside the artifact; the first Desktop run must confirm they draw.
check: Page renders with the CDN blocked
Dates are UTC west of Greenwich
